chunks: Ali ibn Abdillah al-Warraq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated, from his father, from Rabi' ibn Abdurrahman, who said:

I swear by God that Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) was among those who discerned (al-mutawassimin); he knew those who would stop at him after his death and deny the Imamate after his Imamate. Therefore, he suppressed his anger towards them and did not reveal to them what he knew about them, so he was called al-Kazim (the Suppresser of Anger) because of that.

key_terms.الْكَازِمَ: The one who suppresses (anger), a title of Musa ibn Ja'far
key_terms.الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ: Those who discern or perceive hidden realities
key_terms.يَقِفُ عَلَيْهِ: To stop at or accept the Imamate of a specific Imam

ai.seo_question: Why is Musa ibn Ja'far called al-Kazim and what does it mean he was among the mutawassimin?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* elucidates the etymology of 'al-Kazim' by linking it to Musa ibn Ja'far’s (AS) divine foresight (*al-mutawassimin*) regarding the Waqifites who would halt at his death. It highlights his strategic patience in concealing this knowledge to avoid premature conflict, thereby transforming a potential source of anger into a defining attribute of his Imamate. This context underscores the Shia scholarly view that his silence was an active, knowledgeable restraint rather than mere passivity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-1 Ali ibn Abdillah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdillah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Rabi ibn Abdurrahman,

“I swear by God that Musa ibn Ja’far (s) was extremely intelligent. He knew those who will stop believing in Divine Leadership after him, and not accept the next Divine Leaders. However, he (s) quenched his anger and did not divulge what he (s) knew about them. That is why he (s) is called ’Kadhim.“
